description: Authentication backend must properly handle user registration and login with correct JWT_SECRET_KEY configuration and database query handling

criticalIssuesIdentified.issue: JWT_SECRET_KEY not configured in Kubernetes deployment
criticalIssuesIdentified.impact: JWT tokens use weak default secret ('development-secret-key-change-in-production'), causing token validation failures and security vulnerabilities
criticalIssuesIdentified.evidence: Lines 43-47 show SECRET_KEY environment variable is commented out, no JWT_SECRET_KEY configured

criticalIssuesIdentified.issue: Registration returns 400 'Email already registered' for all attempts
criticalIssuesIdentified.impact: Users cannot create new accounts, blocking onboarding flow
criticalIssuesIdentified.evidence: SurrealDB query result parsing may return false positives due to nested result structure

criticalIssuesIdentified.issue: Login returns 401 'Invalid email or password' for all attempts
criticalIssuesIdentified.impact: Users cannot authenticate even with valid credentials
criticalIssuesIdentified.evidence: User query may fail to parse nested SurrealDB result structure or password verification fails

components.currentBehavior: JWT_SECRET_KEY environment variable is NOT configured. SECRET_KEY is commented out (lines 43-47). Container uses default weak secret from jwt_auth.py
components.desiredBehavior: JWT_SECRET_KEY must be injected from Kubernetes secret with strong random value (>=32 chars)
components.gap: Add environment variable: JWT_SECRET_KEY from secret 'metabob-rpc-api-secrets' key 'jwt-secret-key'

components.currentBehavior: SECRET_KEY = os.getenv('JWT_SECRET_KEY', 'development-secret-key-change-in-production'). Uses weak default if environment variable not set. Logs critical warning but doesn't fail in non-production mode
components.desiredBehavior: JWT_SECRET_KEY must be configured via environment variable with strong secret (>=32 chars). Should fail fast if weak secret detected
components.gap: Environment variable JWT_SECRET_KEY must be set in Kubernetes deployment
components.note: Code is correct - issue is deployment configuration

components.currentBehavior: Query: 'SELECT user_id FROM users WHERE email = $email'. Checks if existing and len(existing) > 0 and len(existing[0]) > 0. May return false positives due to SurrealDB result structure parsing
components.desiredBehavior: Should correctly parse SurrealDB result structure and only reject if user actually exists. Handle nested result formats: [{'status': 'OK', 'result': [...]}] or [[...]] or [...]
components.gap: Add proper result parsing with structure analysis like in login endpoint (lines 125-147)

components.currentBehavior: Creates org, user, user_organizations junction, generates JWT token. Flow appears correct with proper bcrypt hashing and UUID generation
components.desiredBehavior: Same as current - this part is correctly implemented

components.component: Login Endpoint - User Query and Password Verification
components.currentBehavior: Queries user by email, handles multiple SurrealDB result formats (lines 125-147), verifies password with bcrypt. Has comprehensive structured logging. Password verification uses verify_password() from jwt_auth.py
components.desiredBehavior: Same as current - comprehensive result parsing and password verification is correct
components.gap: None - implementation is correct. If login fails, issue is likely: 1) JWT_SECRET_KEY mismatch causing token validation issues, 2) Test user not seeded in database, or 3) Password hash mismatch

components.currentBehavior: Calls create_access_token(user_id, email, org_id, role) and create_refresh_token(user_id). Uses SECRET_KEY from jwt_auth.py for JWT encoding
components.desiredBehavior: Same as current - token generation is correct. Tokens must use strong SECRET_KEY
components.gap: JWT_SECRET_KEY must be properly configured in deployment
components.note: Code is correct - issue is deployment configuration

components.currentBehavior: Uses official surrealdb-py AsyncSurreal client. Executes queries with parameter binding. Has retry logic for 401 auth errors. Returns nested result structures
components.desiredBehavior: Same as current - client is correctly implemented
components.gap: None - SurrealDB client is working correctly

dataFlow.registration: Frontend POST /auth/register → cloud_auth.py:register() → 1) Check email exists (line 435-436) → 2) Hash password (line 445) → 3) Generate IDs (lines 448-449) → 4) Create organization (line 459) → 5) Create user (line 473) → 6) Create user_organizations junction (line 482) → 7) Generate JWT token with SECRET_KEY (line 485-490) → 8) Return RegisterResponse
dataFlow.login: Frontend POST /auth/login → cloud_auth.py:login() → 1) Query user by email (line 91) → 2) Parse nested result structure (lines 125-147) → 3) Verify password with bcrypt (line 190) → 4) Generate JWT tokens with SECRET_KEY (lines 241-248) → 5) Update last_login_at (lines 282-284) → 6) Query user organizations (line 316) → 7) Return LoginResponse with token and user data
dataFlow.jwtValidation: Frontend request with Authorization: Bearer <token> → jwt_auth.py:decode_token() → jwt.decode(token, SECRET_KEY) → If SECRET_KEY mismatch → ExpiredSignatureError or PyJWTError → HTTPException 401 Unauthorized

currentIssues.issue1: JWT_SECRET_KEY not set in K8s → uses weak default → tokens signed with weak secret → security vulnerability
currentIssues.issue2: Registration email check returns false positives → may be checking len(existing[0]) on nested structure incorrectly → always returns 'Email already registered'
currentIssues.issue3: Login may fail if: a) test user not in database, b) password hash mismatch, c) JWT_SECRET_KEY mismatch causing downstream token issues

rootCauseAnalysis.primaryCause: JWT_SECRET_KEY environment variable not configured in Kubernetes deployment (metabob-apps/charts/metabob-rpc-api/charts/templates/deployment-api.yaml)
rootCauseAnalysis.secondaryCause: Registration endpoint's email duplicate check may have result parsing bug (lacks same robust parsing as login endpoint)
rootCauseAnalysis.impact: Complete authentication failure - users cannot register or login, dashboard unusable
rootCauseAnalysis.securityImplications: Using weak default JWT secret allows token forgery attacks

step1.command: kubectl create secret generic metabob-rpc-api-secrets -n metabob --from-literal=jwt-secret-key=$(openssl rand -hex 32)

step2.action: Add JWT_SECRET_KEY environment variable to deployment
step2.change:
Add after line 42: - name: JWT_SECRET_KEY
  valueFrom:
    secretKeyRef:
      name: metabob-rpc-api-secrets
      key: jwt-secret-key

step3.action: Fix registration endpoint email duplicate check result parsing
step3.change: Add robust result parsing like login endpoint (lines 125-147) to handle nested SurrealDB structures

step4.action: Verify test user exists in database or create seed data
step4.validation: Query SurrealDB: SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = 'test@metabob.com'

step5.action: Deploy updated chart and restart pods
step5.command: helmfile -e default apply && kubectl rollout restart deployment/metabob-rpc-api -n metabob

validationTests.test: Verify JWT_SECRET_KEY is set in pod
validationTests.command: kubectl exec -it deployment/metabob-rpc-api -n metabob -- env | grep JWT_SECRET_KEY

validationTests.expectedResult: 200 OK with token and user data
200 OK with token, user, and organizations data
200 OK with user_id, email, org_id, role

complianceChecks.spec1: JWT_SECRET_KEY properly configured with strong secret (>=32 chars)
complianceChecks.spec2: Registration endpoint validates emails correctly and creates users in SurrealDB
complianceChecks.spec3: Login endpoint verifies credentials, queries users, returns valid JWT tokens
complianceChecks.spec4: User records include bcrypt-hashed passwords, organization linkage, proper timestamps
